EQUIPMENT REQUIRED
To gain an understanding of Time Division Multiplexing (TDM) circuits, you will observe the operation of a typical TDM Multiplexer or Transmitter and a TDM Demultiplexer or Receiver circuits.
INTRODUCTIONM
First the multiplexer circuit is set up and analyzed to produce a TDM signal.
The TDM Demultiplexer circuit is analyzed using the TDM signal from the multiplexer.
The circuits use four information channels and one SYNC pulse channel.
The MC14051 chip is used as the multiplexer and demultiplexer.
The other circuits use standard digital counters, op-amps, and logic gates.
Other types of chips may be used for multiplexing and demultiplexing. The chips used in this lesson are typical and give you a basic understanding of TDM system operation and maintenance techniques.

TDM TRANSMITTERSTLE
In this experiment, you will observe the operation and measure signals in a typical TDM transmitter circuit.
EXPERIMENT
The transmitter circuit is contained on PC130-305 and consists of the components necessary to support the multiplexer chip (IC2).
Four information signals are applied through individual operational amplifiers in IC1.
The gain of each information input is independently set by R22 through R25.
The output of the amplifiers are applied through a bias network to the multiplexer inputs X1 through X4.
Biasing of each information signal places them at a positive level.
The SYNC pulse input is X0 and is ground. This will make the SYNC pulse different from a positive information signal on X1 through X4.
Inputs X5 through X7 are not used and are grounded. The inhibit input is also grounded to allow the chip to operate.
The TDM output is taken from pin 3, through a bias network and level control. This places the SYNC pulse to a negative level.
The control circuit is a MC14040B counter..................
The Q1 through Q3 outputs of the counter are used as the A, B and C inputs to the multiplexer.
The counter also uses the Q1 and Q3 outputs as a reset signal.
When the count is 101, the fifth count, the IC4c LOW output is inverted to a HIGH in IC4d. The HIGH resets the counter.
Remember, only five inputs are used, X0 is the SYNC pulse and X1 through X4 are the information inputs.
The counter counts from 000 to 101 to select one of the five inputs and then starts over.
The clock circuit is formed by IC4a and IC4b, a schmitt trigger.

R22 through R25 are the four information input signal adjustments.
R15 is the clock or sample rate adjustment.

EXPERIMENT
BVBTCRDPE
The receiver circuit is contained on PC130-306 and consists of the components necessary to support the demultiplexer.
The TDM signal is sent through a bias network and SYNC detector Q1, to a level control R1 then, to the demultiplexer IC4.
The demultiplexer uses the X1 through X4 as the outputs. X0 is not used because it is the SYNC pulse and not information.
Each output of the demultiplexer is applied to individual operational amplifiers through a bias network.
R26 through R29 control the gains of each amplifier independently.
The clock circuit is formed by IC2b and IC2c and set by R10.
BVBTCRDPE
The control circuit is a MC14040B counter..................
Note that the outputs of Q3 through Q6 are used.
The Q3 output drives the inhibit input of the demultiplexer. It is used to set up guard times.
The Q4, Q5 and Q6 outputs control the A, B and C inputs to the demultiplexer.
When the count is 0000, the demultiplexer is not inhibited and selects the X0 output, SYNC pulse.
When the count becomes 1000, the demultiplexer is inhibited and the operation of the chip is disabled.
When the count becomes 0100, the demultiplexer is not inhibited and selects the X1 output.
When the count becomes 1100, the demultiplexer is inhibited and disables the X1 output.
When the count becomes 0010, the demultiplexer is not inhibited and selects the X2 output.
When the count becomes 1010, the demultiplexer is inhibited and disables the X2 output.
Remember, when Q3 is HIGH, the demultiplexer is disabled.
BVBTCRDPE
The SYNC detector consists of Q1, IC2a and IC2d............
When the TDM input is a positive level, meaning that information is being received, Q1 turns ON producing a LOW to IC2a.
The LOW on IC2a produces a LOW signal out of the schmitt trigger of IC2a and IC2d, IC3 is not reset.
When the TDM input is a negative level, meaning that a SYNC pulse is being received, Q1 turns OFF producing a HIGH to IC2a.
The HIGH on IC2a produces a HIGH signal out of the schmitt trigger of IC2a and IC2d, IC3 is reset.
The counter circuit gets reset whenever a SYNC pulse is received.
